Both answers cover the required path, dependency boundary, 304 header/body cleanup, tests, and bounded three-request verification. B is more precise and easier to continue from: it gives separate exact dependency locations, cites the local stringify implementation and weak-ETag test, and clearly notes that a preexisting ETag is preserved but still participates in freshness evaluation. statements: res.json() serializes the value and delegates to res.send().
res.send() generates an ETag when none is set and checks req.fresh.
The If-None-Match freshness comparison is delegated to a dependency rather than implemented in Express.
On a fresh request the status becomes 304, body-related headers are removed, and an empty body is sent.
Verification is grounded in the existing tests (test/res.send.js) or request headers.
